title: A section of a square-zero quotient splits the conormal map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $C$ a commutative $R$-algebra, and $\pi:C\to C'$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $K$ satisfies $K^2=0$. Suppose $\pi$ has a right inverse $\sigma:C'\to C$ that is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras ($\pi\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_{C'}$). Then the $C$-linear map $$\delta:K\longrightarrow C'\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R},\qquad \delta(x)=1\otimes\mathrm dx$$ ($\Omega_{C/R}$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]) has a $C$-linear left inverse $\tau$, $\tau\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_K$. In particular $\delta$ is injective with image a direct summand. (If $\pi$ is surjective, $K$ and $C'\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}$ are $C'$-modules and $C$-linear maps between them are $C'$-linear.)
